				<td valign="bottom" style="width:04.10%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;background-color: #FFFFFF;height:12.75pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-align:right;" nowrap="nowrap"><div style="float:left"></div>116&nbsp;
				</td>
			</tr>
			<tr>
				<td valign="top" style="width:14.12%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;background-color: #FFFFFF;height:12.75pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0.05pt;font-family:Times New Roman;overflow: hidden;font-size:0pt;">
						<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font></p>
				</td>

					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0.05pt;font-family:Times New Roman;overflow: hidden;font-size:0pt;">

				</td>

			<tr>
				<td colspan="2" valign="top" style="width:95.90%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;background-color: #FFFFFF;height:15.00pt;padding:0pt;">

						<font style="display: inline;">Signatures</font></p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">1</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">GLOSSARY OF</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">OIL AND NATURAL GAS</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">TERMS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">API</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;American Petroleum Institute </font><font style="display: inline;">is the main U.S</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> trade association for the oil and natural gas industry</font><font style="display: inline;"> whose functions include establishment and certification of industry standards like the gravity (density) of petroleum.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Basin:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">A l</font><font style="display: inline;">ow area in the Earth&#x2019;s crust in which sediments have accumulated.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Bbl:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;One stock tank barrel, or 42 U.S.&nbsp;gallons liquid volume, used in reference to oil or other liquid hydrocarbons.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Bbl/d:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;One Bbl per day.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Bcf:</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">One billion cubic feet of natural gas.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Boe:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">One barrel of oil equivalent, calculated by converting natural gas to oil equivalent barrels at a ratio of six Mcf of natural gas to one Bbl of oil.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Boe/d:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">One Boe per day.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Btu:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">One British thermal unit, the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of a one-pound mass of water by one degree Fahrenheit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Completion:</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The i</font><font style="display: inline;">nstallation of permanent equipment for production of oil or gas, or, in the </font><font style="display: inline;">case of a dry well, to report</font><font style="display: inline;"> to the appropriate authority the well has been abandoned.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Condensate:</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">A mixture of hydrocarbons that exists in the gaseous phase at original reservoir temperature and pressure, but that, when produced, is in the liquid phase at surface pressure and temperature.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">D</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">eveloped Acreage:</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The number of acres which are allocated or assignable to producing wells or wells capable of production.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Developed </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">O</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">il and </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Natural G</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">as </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">R</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">eserves:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Reserves of any category that can be expected to be recovered:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">through existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods or in which the cost of the required equipment is relatively minor compared with the cost of a new well, and</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">through installed extraction equipment and infrastructure operational at the time of the reserves estimate if the extraction is by means not involving a well.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Development</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">C</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">osts</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Costs incurred to obtain access to proved reserves and to provide facilities for extracting, treating, gathering and storing oil and gas.&nbsp;More specifically, development costs, including depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of development activities, are costs incurred to:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">gain access to and prepare well locations for drilling, including surveying well locations for the purpose of determining specific development drilling sites, clearing ground, draining water, road building and relocating public roads, gas lines and power lines, to the extent necessary in developing the proved reserves; </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">drill and equip development wells, development-type stratigraphic test wells and service wells, including the costs of platforms and well equipment such as casing, tubing, pumping equipment and the wellhead assembly; </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">acquire, construct and install production facilities such as lease flow lines, separators, treaters, heaters, manifolds, measuring devices, production storage tanks, natural gas cycling and processing plants, and central utility and waste disposal systems; and </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">provide improved recovery systems.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">2</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Development Project</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">:</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The means by which petroleum resources are brought to the status of economically producible.&nbsp;&nbsp;As examples, the development of a single reservoir or field, an incremental development in a producing field, or the integrated development of a group of several fields and associated facilities with a common ownership may constitute a development project</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Development Well:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">A well drilled within the proved area of an oil or natural gas reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be productive.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Dry Hole or Well:</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">A well found to be incapable of producing hydrocarbons in sufficient quantities such that proceeds from the sale of such production would exceed production expenses and taxes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Economically Producible</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">:</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> A resource which generates revenue that exceeds, or is reasonably expected to exceed, the costs of the operation</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Enhanced Recovery:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Any method used to drive oil from reservoirs into a well in excess of that which could be produced through natural reservoir pressure, energy, or drive.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Exploitation:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">A development or other project which may target proven or unproven reserves (such as probable or possible reserves), but which generally has a lower risk than that associated with exploration projects.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">FASB</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Financial Accounting Standards Board</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Field:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">An area consisting of a single reservoir or multiple reservoirs, all grouped on or related to the same individual geological structural feature and/or stratigraphic condition. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The field name refers to the surface area, although it may refer to both the surface and the underground productive formations.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">This definition has been abbreviated from the applicable definitions contained in Rule 4-10(a)(2-4) of Regulation S-X.</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Novate:&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">To substitute by mutual agreement one obligation for another, such as the substitution of one party to a contract for another, with the intent to extinguish the old obligation.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, the substitution of one party to a </font><font style="display: inline;">derivative contract </font><font style="display: inline;">for another party upon </font><font style="display: inline;">mutual consent of the original counterparties and the concurrence of the new party.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Proved Developed R</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">eserves:</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;Proved reserves that can be expected to be recovered from existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">This definition has been abbreviated from the applicable definitions contained in Rule 4-10(a)(2-4) of Regulation S-X.</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Proved R</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">eserves:</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;&nbsp;Those quantities of oil and gas, which, by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;"> from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> government regulations&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;"> prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The project to extract the hydrocarbons must have commenced or the operator must be reasonably certain that it will commence the project within a reasonable time. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">This definition has been abbreviated from the applicable definitions contained in Rule 4-10(a)(2-4) of Regulation S-X.</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Recompletion:</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;&nbsp;The </font><font style="display: inline;">operation whereby a completion in one zone is abandoned in order to attempt a completion in a different zone within the existing wellbore.&nbsp; </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Reservoir:</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">A porous and permeable underground formation containing a natural accumulation of producible oil and/or natural gas that is confined by impermeable rock or water barriers and is individual and separate from other reserves.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Spacing:</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;&nbsp;The distance between wells producing from the same reservoir. Spacing is often expressed in terms of acres (e.g., 40-acre spacing) and is often established by regulatory agencies.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Our properties consist of</font><font style="display: inline;"> mature, legacy onshore oil and natural gas reservoirs with long-lived, predictable production profiles.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, our total estimated proved reserves were approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">109.1 </font><font style="display: inline;">MMBoe, of which approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">77</font><font style="display: inline;">% were oil and NGLs and </font><font style="display: inline;">85</font><font style="display: inline;">% were classified as proved developed reserves.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> As of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">, our estimated proved reserves had a standardized measure </font><font style="display: inline;">of</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;$</font><font style="display: inline;">2.0 b</font><font style="display: inline;">illion.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;As of December 31, 2013, we produced from 5,668 g</font><font style="display: inline;">ross (</font><font style="display: inline;">3,270</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">net) wells</font><font style="display: inline;"> across our properties, with an average working interest of 57.7</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp; </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Fund is a collection of limited partnerships formed by two of the co-founders of Quantum Energy Partners and Don Wolf, the Chairman of the Board of our general partner, for the purpose of acquiring mature, legacy producing oil and natural gas properties with long-lived production profiles. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The Fund is managed by Quantum Resources Management, a full service management company formed to manage the oil and natural gas interests of the Fund.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Our general partner has entered into a </font><font style="display: inline;">Services Agreement (the&#x201C;S</font><font style="display: inline;">ervices </font><font style="display: inline;">A</font><font style="display: inline;">greement</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;"> with Quantum Resources Management in which Quantum Resources Management has agreed to provide the administrative and acquisition advisory services that we believe are necessary to allow our general partner to manage, operate and grow our business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 27.35pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Fund is contractually committed to providing us with opportunities to purchase additional proved reserves in future periods under specified circumstances</font><font style="display: inline;">. Under the terms of the</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">O</font><font style="display: inline;">mnibus </font><font style="display: inline;">A</font><font style="display: inline;">greement</font><font style="display: inline;"> (the &#x201D;Omnibus Agreement&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Fund has committed to offer us the first opportunity to purchase properties that it may offer for sale, so long as the properties consist of at least 70% proved developed producing reserves, as measured by value. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 27.35pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 27.35pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Fund will determine whether any group of properties offered for sale meets the 70% threshold, and therefore, whether it is obligated to offer such properties to us.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 70% threshold is a value-weighted determination made by the Fund, acting in good faith pursuant to the terms of our O</font><font style="display: inline;">mnibus </font><font style="display: inline;">A</font><font style="display: inline;">greement</font><font style="display: inline;">, and is subject to a number of subjective assumptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, other than the Fund&#x2019;s obligation to act in good faith, there are no additional safeguards in place to prevent the Fund from selecting a subset of assets that do not meet this standard or allocating value in a manner where the proved developed producing assets are below the 70% threshold.&nbsp;&nbsp;Given the Fund&#x2019;s significant ownership in us, we believe there is a sufficient economic incentive to deter the Fund from structuring its asset dispositions in an attempt to circumvent our contractual rights under the O</font><font style="display: inline;">mnibus </font><font style="display: inline;">A</font><font style="display: inline;">greement</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 27.35pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 27.35pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We believe the Fund has a vested interest in our ability to increase our reserves and production since it holds an </font><font style="display: inline;">aggregate </font><font style="display: inline;">29.2</font><font style="display: inline;">% limited partner interest in us including all of our Class C preferred units as of </font><font style="display: inline;">March 2,</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Except as provided in the </font><font style="display: inline;">O</font><font style="display: inline;">mnibus </font><font style="display: inline;">A</font><font style="display: inline;">greement</font><font style="display: inline;">, as described above, the Fund has no obligation</font><font style="display: inline;"> to offer additional properties to us.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the Fund fails to present us with, or successfully competes against us for acquisition opportunities, then we may not be able to replace or increase our estimated proved reserves, which would adversely affect our cash flow from operations and our ability to make cash distributions to our unitholders.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 27.35pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 27.35pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Quantum Energy </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Partners</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 27.35pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 27.35pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Quantum Energy Partners is a private equity firm that was founded in 1998 to make investments in the energy sector.&nbsp;&nbsp;Two of the co-founders and certain other employees of Quantum Energy Partners own interests in the general partner of the Fund.&nbsp;&nbsp;Two of the co-founders also own interests in our general partner.&nbsp;&nbsp;The employees of Quantum Energy Partners are experienced energy professionals with expertise in finance and operations and broad technical skills in the oil and natural gas business.&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the business of Quantum Energy Partners, these employees review a large number of potential acquisitions and are involved in decisions relating to the acquisition and disposition of oil and natural gas assets by the various portfolio companies in which Quantum Energy Partners owns interests.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although there is no obligation to do so, to the extent not inconsistent with their fiduciary duties and obligations to the investors and other parties involved with Quantum Energy Partners, Quantum Energy Partners may refer to us or allow us to participate in new acquisitions by its portfolio companies and may cause its portfolio companies to sell oil and natural </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Ark-La-Tex</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Ark-La-Tex area includes properties located in east Texas, northern Louisiana and southern Arkansas. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">These properties produce from formations such as the Cotton Valley Sand, Haynesville Sand, Woodbine Sand and Smackover Carbonate at depths ranging from 1</font><font style="display: inline;">,000 to 11,000 feet.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">During 2013, we acquired an additional interest in the East Texas Oil Field.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2013, we invested $</font><font style="display: inline;">27.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in capital in this area</font><font style="display: inline;">, primarily on recompletions, returning wells to production, artificial lift enhancements and facility upgrades in the Dorcheat Macedonia, East Texas Oil Field, Gladewater, Neches and Shongaloo fields.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2013, we drilled 2 net (2 gross) wells in the Ark-La-Tex area, both in the East Texas Oil Field.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The East Texas Oil Field is a significant field which constituted approximately 17% of our estimated proved reserves as of December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Partnership&#x2019;s production from the East Texas Oil Field is presented for the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012, and 2011.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Permian Basin</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Permian Basin area includes properties located in west Texas and southeast New Mexico and produces from a variety of reservoirs such as the San Andres, Grayburg and Clearfork formations at depths ranging from 4,000 to 11,000 feet.&nbsp;&nbsp;Many of these properties are under secondary recovery waterflood operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;During 2013, we invested $48.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in capital in the Permian Basin</font><font style="display: inline;">, primarily on development drilling in the Blineberry-Drinkard, Garden City South, Turner Gregory, and Wasson fields.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2013, we drilled or participated in the drilling of 1</font><font style="display: inline;">8</font><font style="display: inline;"> net (66 gross) wells in the Permian Basin.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other Permian Basin capital was spent on recompletions, artificial lift enhancements and facility upgrades, primarily in our Fuhrman Mascho, East Corrigan, G P M, North Cowden and Turner Gregory fields.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During 2014, we expect to invest approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">40</font><font style="display: inline;"> million </font><font style="display: inline;">in capital in the Permian Basin, primarily on further development drilling, recompletions, workovers, and facility upgrades.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Internal Controls.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Our proved reserves, which are estimated at the well or unit level, are compiled for reporting purposes by Quantum Resources Management&#x2019;s corporate reservoir engineering staff, all of whom are independent of Quantum Resources Management operating teams.&nbsp;&nbsp;Quantum Resources Management maintains internal evaluations of our reserves in a secure reserve engineering database.&nbsp;&nbsp;The corporate reservoir engineering staff interacts with Quantum Resources Management&#x2019;s internal petroleum engineers and geoscience professionals in each of our operating areas and with operating, accounting and marketing employees to obtain the necessary data for the reserves estimation process.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reserves are reviewed and approved internally by our senior management on a semi-annual basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our reserve estimates are prepared </font><font style="display: inline;">annually </font><font style="display: inline;">by our independent third-party reserve engineers, </font><font style="display: inline;">Netherland, Sewell &amp; Associates, Inc.</font><font style="display: inline;">, for the year ended December 31, 2013 and Miller and Lents, L</font><font style="display: inline;">td</font><font style="display: inline;">., for the years ended December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2012 and 2011</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our internal professional staff works closely with </font><font style="display: inline;">our independent third-party reserve engineers</font><font style="display: inline;"> to ensure the integrity, accuracy and timeliness of data that is furnished to them for their reserve estimation process.&nbsp;&nbsp;All of the reserve information maintained in our secure reserve engineering database is provided to the external engineers.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we provide </font><font style="display: inline;">our independent third-party reserve engineers</font><font style="display: inline;"> other pertinent data, such as seismic information, geologic maps, well logs, production tests, material balance calculations, well performance data, operating procedures and relevant economic criteria.&nbsp;&nbsp;We make all requested information, as well as our pertinent personnel, available to the external engineers as part of their evaluation of our reserves.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Development of Proved Undeveloped Reserves</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Recovery of proved undeveloped (</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">PUD</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;">) reserves requires significant capital expenditures and successful drilling operations.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The reserve data assumes that we can and will make these expenditures and conduct these operations successfully, but future events, including commodity price changes, may cause these assumptions to change. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">In addition, estimates of PUD reserves and proved developed non-producing reserves are inherently subject to greater uncertainties than estimates of proved developed producing reserves.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> For further discussion of our reserves, see Part II, Item&nbsp;8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Supplemental Oil and Natural Gas Information.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">We currently have 245 proved undeveloped locations, including 69 injection wells for secondary and tertiary recovery operations.</font>

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In our December 31, 2013 reserve report, the amounts estimated to be spent over the next five years to develop our consolidated PUD reserves are $215 million or an average of $43 million per year.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amounts estimated to be spent to develop our PUD reserves are a result of our capital focus to develop our core projects.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amounts and timing of these expenditures will depend on a number of factors, including actual drilling results, service costs and commodity prices.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Title to Properties</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Prior to completing an acquisition of producing oil and natural gas properties, we perform title reviews on significant leases, and depending on the materiality of properties, we may obtain a title opinion or review previously obtained title opinions.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, title examinations have been obtained on a significant portion of our properties.&nbsp;&nbsp;After an acquisition, we review the assignments from the seller for scrivener&#x2019;s and other errors and execute and record corrective assignments as necessary.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As is customary in the oil and natural gas industry, we initially conduct only a cursory review of the titles to our properties on which we do not have proved reserves.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to the commencement of drilling operations on those properties, we conduct a thorough title examination and perform curative work with respect to significant defects.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent title opinions or other investigations reflect title defects on those properties, we are typically responsible for curing any title defects at our own expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;We generally will not commence drilling operations on a property until we have cured any material title defects on such property.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We believe that we have satisfactory title to all of our material assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although title to these properties is subject to encumbrances in some cases, such as customary interests generally retained in connection with the acquisition of real property, customary royalty interests and contract terms and restrictions, liens under operating agreements, liens related to environmental liabilities associated with historical operations, liens for current taxes and other burdens, easements, restrictions and minor encumbrances customary in the oil and natural gas industry, we believe that none of these liens, restrictions, easements, burdens or encumbrances will materially detract from the value of these properties or from our interest in these properties or materially interfere with our use of these properties in the operation of our business.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we believe that we have obtained sufficient rights-of-way grants and permits from public authorities and private parties for us to operate our business in all material respects as described in this Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">We operated approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">93</font><font style="display: inline;">% of our assets as determined by value, based on standardized measure as of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> We design and manage the development, recompletion or workover</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> for all of the wells we operate</font><font style="display: inline;"> including the </font><font style="display: inline;">supervis</font><font style="display: inline;">ion</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">of </font><font style="display: inline;">operation and maintenance activities.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> We do not own the drilling rigs or other oil field services equipment used for drilling or maintaining wells on the properties we operate.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Independent contractors provide all the equipment and personnel associated with these activities.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Pursuant to our general partner&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;">Services Agreement</font><font style="display: inline;">, Quantum Resources Management provides certain administrative services to us. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Quantum Resources Management employs production and reservoir engineers, geologists and other specialists, as well as field personnel</font><font style="display: inline;"> that may perform work on our behalf</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Cambria Math;">&#x2012;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Services Agreement</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">We charge the non</font><font style="display: inline;">-</font><font style="display: inline;">operating partners a contractual administrative overhead charge for operating the wells.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Some of our non-operated wells are managed by third-party operators who are typically independent oil and natural gas companies.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Customer A, Customer B, and Customer C</font><font style="display: inline;"> purchase oil production pursuant to existing marketing agreements with terms that are currently on &#x201C;evergreen&#x201D; status and renew on a month-to-month basis until either party gives 30-day advance written notice of non-renewal.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">If we were to lose any one of our customers, the loss could temporarily delay production and sale of our oil and natural gas in the related producing region.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we were to lose any single customer, we believe we could identify a substitute customer to purchase the impacted production volumes.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, if one or more of our larger customers ceased purchasing oil or natural gas altogether, the loss could have a detrimental effect on our production volumes in general and on our ability to find substitute customers to purchase our production volumes.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">We have no commitments to deliver a fixed and determinable quantity of our oil or natural gas production in the </font><font style="display: inline;">near future under our existing contracts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Derivatives Activities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We enter into commodity </font><font style="display: inline;">derivative contracts with unaffiliated third parties to achieve more predictable cash flows and to reduce our exposure to short-term fluctuations in oil and natural gas prices.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Our</font><font style="display: inline;"> current commodity derivative contracts</font><font style="display: inline;"> include fixed price swaps, basis swaps, and collars on future oil production at WTI and LLS prices, fixed price swaps and basis swaps on future natural gas production</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">with NYMEX prices, natural gas puts, collars on future natural gas production with Henry Hub prices and floors on future natural gas production with Henry Hub prices.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Periodically, we enter into interest rate swaps to mitigate exposure to market rate fluctuations by converting variable interest rates (such as those </font><font style="display: inline;">i</font><font style="display: inline;">n our </font><font style="display: inline;">c</font><font style="display: inline;">redit </font><font style="display: inline;">facility</font><font style="display: inline;">) to fixed interest rates.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> It is our policy to enter into derivative contracts, including interest rate swaps, only with counterparties that are creditworthy financial institutions deemed by management as competent and competitive market makers.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> We will continue to evaluate the benefit of employing derivatives in the future. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">See </font><font style="display: inline;">Part II, </font><font style="display: inline;">Item&nbsp;7A. </font><font style="display: inline;">Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk</font><font style="display: inline;"> for additional information.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We operate in a highly competitive environment for acquiring properties, leasing acreage, contracting for drilling equipment and securing trained personnel.&nbsp;&nbsp;Many of our competitors possess and employ financial, technical and personnel resources substantially greater than ours, which can be particularly important in the areas in which we operate.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, our competitors may be able to pay more for productive oil and natural gas properties and exploratory prospects, as well as evaluate, bid for and purchase a greater number of properties and prospects than our financial or personnel resources permit.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our ability to acquire additional properties and to find and develop reserves will depend on our ability to evaluate and select suitable properties and to consummate transactions in a highly competitive environment.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, there is substantial competition for capital available for investment in the oil and natural gas industry.&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:0.05pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
