		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On </font><font style="display: inline;">August 6, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, we closed the acquisition of primarily oil properties located in East Texas (the &#x201C;2013 East Texas Acquisition&#x201D;) from a private seller for </font><font style="display: inline;">$107.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments, using funds drawn on our revolving credit facility. The acquired properties (the &#x201C;2013 East Texas Properties&#x201D;) had estimated proved reserves of </font><font style="display: inline;">5.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> MMBoe as of the date of the acquisition utilizing SEC case pricing. The acquisition had an effective date of </font><font style="display: inline;">June 1, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">. The costs associated with the 2013 East Texas Acquisition of </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million are recorded in &#x201C;Acquisition and transaction costs&#x201D; on our consolidated statements of operations for the year ended December 31, 2013. In connection with the 2013 East Texas Acquisition, we assumed an estimated environmental liability of </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million. Refer to Note 11 &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Commitments and Contingencies </font><font style="display: inline;">for further details. Since the closing date, revenues of </font><font style="display: inline;">$60</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and production expenses of </font><font style="display: inline;">$15.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million related to the operation of the 2013 East Texas Properties are included in our consolidated statements of operations for year ended December 31, 2013.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In connection with the 2013 East Texas Acquisition, we also acquired a </font><font style="display: inline;">32%</font><font style="display: inline;"> interest in ETSWDC giving us control of ETSWDC as we previously owned </font><font style="display: inline;">24%</font><font style="display: inline;">. During the fourth quarter 2013 we acquired an additional </font><font style="display: inline;">3%</font><font style="display: inline;"> from another seller</font><font style="display: inline;"> giving us a 59</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> ownership interest as of December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of the closing date of the 2013 East Texas Acquisition, we have a controlling interest in the ETSWDC and have consolidated ETSWDC into our consolidated financial statements. In addition, our previous ownership in ETSWDC was remeasured to fair value on the acquisition date resulting in a gain of </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million recognized in &#x201C;Other income (expense)&#x201D; in our consolidated statements of operations. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">On </font><font style="display: inline;">December 4, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;"> we closed the East Texas Oil Field Acquisition</font><font style="display: inline;"> (the &#x201C;2012 East Texas Acquisition")</font><font style="display: inline;">. We acquired the East Texas Oil Field Properties</font><font style="display: inline;"> (the &#x201C;2012 East Texas Properties&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;"> for $</font><font style="display: inline;">214.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in cash </font><font style="display: inline;">after</font><font style="display: inline;"> customary purchase price adjustments. The acquired properties had estimated proved reserves of </font><font style="display: inline;">10.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> MMBoe as of December 31, 2011 utilizing SEC case pricing. The acquisition had an effective date </font><font style="display: inline;">of </font><font style="display: inline;">November 1, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The costs associated with the </font><font style="display: inline;">2012 </font><font style="display: inline;">East Texas Acquisition of $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million are recorded in &#x201C;Acquisition and transaction costs&#x201D; in the consolidated statement of operations for the year ended December 31, 2012. The </font><font style="display: inline;">2012 </font><font style="display: inline;">East Texas Acquisition qualified as a business combination and was accounted for under the purchase method of accounting. The fair value measurements of the oil and gas properties and asset retirement obligations were measured using valuation techniques and unobservable inputs that convert future cash flows to a single discounted amount.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the year ended December 31, 2013 we received </font><font style="display: inline;">$8.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in proceeds from the sale of available-for-sale securities with a realized loss of less than </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We evaluate securities for other than temporary impairment on a quarterly basis and more frequently when economic or market concerns warrant such an evaluation. The unrealized losses above have been outstanding for less than six</font><font style="display: inline;"> months</font><font style="display: inline;">. We have evaluated the unrealized losses above and have determined that these losses do not represent an other than temporary impairment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">NOTE </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">6</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;"> &#x2014; FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our financial instruments, including cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable and accounts payable, are carried at cost, which approximates fair value due to the short-term maturity of these instruments. Our financial and non-financial assets and liabilities that are being measured on a recurring basis are measured and reported at fair value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date (exit price). GAAP establishes a three-tier fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used to measure fair value. The hierarchy gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1 measurements) and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs (Level 3 measurements). The three levels of fair value hierarchy are as follows:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 94.5pt;text-indent: -40.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">F</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">20</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 94.5pt;text-indent: -40.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Level 1 -</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Defined as inputs such as unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 94.5pt;text-indent: -40.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Level 2</font><font style="display: inline;"> - </font><font style="display: inline;">Defined as inputs other than quoted prices in active markets that are either directly or indirectly observable for the asset or liability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 94.5pt;text-indent: -40.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Level 3 -</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Defined as unobservable inputs for use when little or no market data</font><font style="display: inline;"> exists, therefore requiring am</font><font style="display: inline;">enity to develop its own assumptions for the asset or liability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Commodity Derivative Instruments </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The fair value of the commodity derivative instruments are estimated using a combined income and market valuation methodology based upon forward commodity price</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> and volatility curves. The curves are obtained from independent pricing services reflecting broker market quotes.</font><font style="display: inline;"> We validate the data provided by independent pricing services by comparing such pricing against other third party pricing data.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Interest Rate Derivative Instruments </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The fair value of the interest rate derivative instruments are estimated using a combined income and market valuation methodology based upon forward interest rates and volatility curves. The curves are obtained from independent pricing services reflecting broker market quotes.</font><font style="display: inline;"> We validate the data provided by independent pricing services by comparing such pricing against other third party pricing data.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Available for Sale Securities</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; The fair value of the available for sale securities are estimated using actual trade data, broker/dealer quotes, and other similar data, which are obtained from quoted market prices, independent pricing vendors, or other sources. We validate the data provided by independent pricing services to make assessments and determinations as to the ultimate valuation of its investment portfolio by comparing such pricing against other third party pricing data. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We utilize the most observable inputs available for the valuation technique utilized. The financial assets and liabilities are classified in their entirety based on the lowest level of input that is of significance to the fair value measurement. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The following table sets forth, by level within the hierarchy, the fair value of our financial assets and liabilities that were accounted for at fair value on a recurri</font><font style="display: inline;">ng basis as of December 31, 2013 and 2012</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> All fair values reflected below and on the consolidated balance sheet have been adjusted for nonperformance.</font>
		</p>

					<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;height:1.00pt;overflow:hidden;font-size:0pt;">

				</td>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:02.02%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;background-color: #FFFFFF;height:1.00pt;padding:0pt;">

						&nbsp;</p>

						&nbsp;</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revolving Credit Facility </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The fair value of our </font><font style="display: inline;">credit facility</font><font style="display: inline;"> debt depends primarily on the current active market LIBOR. The carrying value of our </font><font style="display: inline;">credit facility</font><font style="display: inline;"> debt as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> approximates fair value based on the current LIBOR and is classified as a Level 2 input in the fair value hierarchy. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Derivative Premiums &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;">The</font><font style="display: inline;"> fair value of the deferred premiums on our commodity derivatives is based on the current active market LIBOR.&nbsp;&nbsp;The carrying value of the premiums as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> approximates fair value based on the current LIBOR and is classified as a Level 2 input in the fair value hierarchy.&nbsp;&nbsp;Refer to N</font><font style="display: inline;">ote 7</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Derivative Activities</font><font style="display: inline;"> for further information on the derivative premiums. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Senior Notes</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; The fair value of the Senior Notes is measured based on inputs from quoted, unadjusted prices from over-the-counter markets for debt instruments. If the Senior Notes had been measured at fair value, we would classify them as Level 1 under the fair value hierarchy. The fair value of the Senior Notes as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013 was $</font><font style="display: inline;">312.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million. </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">There have been no transfers between levels within the fair value measurement hierarchy during </font><font style="display: inline;">the year ended December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have elected not to designate any of our derivatives as hedging instruments. As a result, these derivative instruments are marked to market at the end of each reporting period, and changes in the fair value of the derivatives are recorded as gains or losses in the consolidated statements of operations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Although we have the ability to elect to enter into netting agreements under our derivative instruments with certain of our counterparties, we have presented all asset and liability positions without netting. It is our policy to enter into derivative contracts, including interest rate swaps, only with counterparties that are creditworthy financial institutions deemed by management as competent and competitive market makers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not post collateral under any of these contracts as they are secured under our credit facility. </font><font style="display: inline;">All of our derivative contracts reflected in the consolidated balance sheet have been adjusted for nonperformance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Commodity Derivatives </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our business activities expose us to risks associated with changes in the market price of oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids. As such, future earnings are subject to fluctuations due to changes in the market price of oil and natural gas. We use derivatives to reduce our exposure to changes in the prices of oil and natural gas. Our policies do not permit the use of derivatives for speculative purposes. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the </font><font style="display: inline;">year ended December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, we entered into new oil swap contracts and </font><font style="display: inline;">basis </font><font style="display: inline;">swap contracts with se</font><font style="display: inline;">ttlement dates ranging from 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> through </font><font style="display: inline;">2017</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;All of the new contracts were entered into with </font><font style="display: inline;">counterparties under our revolving credit facility. Additionally, in the fourth quarter of 2013, we converted WTI swaps to LLS swaps.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the year ended December 31, 2012, we </font><font style="display: inline;">terminated certain </font><font style="display: inline;">oil</font><font style="display: inline;"> derivative contracts</font><font style="display: inline;"> that were novated to us in connection with the December 2012 Transferred Properties</font><font style="display: inline;"> which were scheduled to expire at various times </font><font style="display: inline;">in 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> and recorded $</font><font style="display: inline;">5.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million </font><font style="display: inline;">as an adjustment to the purchase price. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The deferred premiums associated with certain of our oil and natural gas derivative instruments are $</font><font style="display: inline;">5.0</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">million</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">$4.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;"> and are classified as other non-current liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> as of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013 and 2012. </font><font style="display: inline;">These deferred premiums will be paid to the counterparty with each monthly settlement (January 2015 &#x2013; December 2017) and recogniz</font><font style="display: inline;">ed as an adjustment of G</font><font style="display: inline;">ain (loss) on </font><font style="display: inline;">commodity </font><font style="display: inline;">derivative </font><font style="display: inline;">contracts, net</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Interest Rate Derivatives </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In an effort to mitigate exposure to changes in market interest rates, we have entered into interest rate swaps that effectively fix the LIBOR component on our outstanding variable rate debt.&nbsp;&nbsp;The changes in the fair value of these instruments are recorded in current earnings. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During </font><font style="display: inline;">2013, we entered into </font><font style="display: inline;">$410</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of </font><font style="display: inline;">new interest rate swaps with termination dates through 2016.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">T</font><font style="display: inline;">he new contracts were entered into with various financial institutions.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On July 31, 2012, we terminated certain interest rate derivative contracts which were scheduled to expire at various times through the fourth quarter 2015 and recorded a $</font><font style="display: inline;">15</font><font style="display: inline;"> million realized loss for the early termination. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Credit Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">By using derivative instruments to hedge exposures to changes in commodity prices and interest rates, when applicable, we are exposed to credit risk. Credit risk is the failure of a counterparty to perform under the terms of the derivative contract. When the fair value of a derivative is in an asset position, the counterparty owes the Partnership, which creates credit risk. We do not receive collateral from our counterparties. The maximum amount of loss to credit risk, based on the gross fair value of our derivative contracts, is $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million as of December 31, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">F</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">23</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Plan Investment Policies and Strategies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The investment policies for </font><font style="display: inline;">the Plans</font><font style="display: inline;"> re</font><font style="display: inline;">flect the funded status of the Plans</font><font style="display: inline;"> and expectations regarding our future ability to make further contributions. Long-term investment goals are to: (1)&nbsp;manage the assets in accordance with the legal requirements of all applicable laws; (2)&nbsp;produce investment returns which meet or exceed the rates of return achievable in the capital markets while maintaining </font><font style="display: inline;">the risk parameters set by the P</font><font style="display: inline;">lans&#x2019; investment committees and protecting the assets from any erosion of purchasing power; and (3)&nbsp;position the portfolios with a long-term risk/return orientation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Historical performance and future expectations suggest that common stocks will provide higher total investment returns than fixed income securities over a long-term investment horizon. Short-term investments are utilized for pension payments, expenses, and other</font><font style="display: inline;"> liquidity needs. As such, the P</font><font style="display: inline;">lan&#x2019;s targeted asset allocation is comprised of</font><font style="display: inline;"> approximately</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">50</font><font style="display: inline;"> percent</font><font style="display: inline;"> equity securities and </font><font style="display: inline;">approximately 50</font><font style="display: inline;"> percent</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">high-yield bonds and </font><font style="display: inline;">other fixed income securities but may be adjusted to better match the plan's liabilities over time as the funded ratio (as defined by the investment policy) changes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Plans&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;"> assets are managed by a third-party investment manager. The investment manager is limited to pursuing the investment strategies regarding asset mix and purchases and sales of securities within the parameters defined in the investment policy guidelines and investment management agreement. Investment performance and risk is measured and monitored on an ongoing basis through </font><font style="display: inline;">annual</font><font style="display: inline;"> investment meetings and periodic </font><font style="display: inline;">cash flow</font><font style="display: inline;"> studies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Expected long-term return on plan assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The overall expected long-term return on plan assets assumption is determined based on an asset rate-of-return modeling tool developed by a third-party investment group. The tool utilizes underlying assumptions based on actual returns by asset category and inflation and </font><font style="display: inline;">takes into account the Plans&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;"> asset allocation</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> to derive an expected long-term rate of return on those assets. Capital market assumptions reflect the long-term capital market outlook. The assumptions for equity and fixed income investments are developed using a building-block approach, reflecting observable inflation information and interest rate information available in the fixed income markets. Long-term assumptions for other asset categories are based on historical results, current market characteristics and the professional judgment of our internal and external investment teams.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value Measurements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Plan assets are measured at fair value. The following provides a description of the valuation techniques em</font><font style="display: inline;">ployed for each major plan asset class at </font><font style="display: inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Cash and cash equivalents &#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Cash and cash equivalents include cash on deposit which are valued using a market approach and are considered Level 1. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Mutual funds</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Investments in mutual funds are valued using a market approach. The shares or units held are traded on the public exchanges and </font><font style="display: inline;">such prices are Level 1 inputs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Pooled funds</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Investments in pooled funds are valued us</font><font style="display: inline;">ing a market approach at the net asset value</font><font style="display: inline;"> of units held, but investment opportunities in such funds are limited to institutional investors on the behalf of defined benefit plans. The various funds consist of either an equity or fixed income investment portfolio with underlying investments held in U.S. and non-U.S. securities. Nearly all of the underlying investments are publicly-traded. The majority of the pooled funds are benchmarked against a relative public index. These are considered Level 2.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Corporate bonds</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Investments in corporate bonds are valued using a market approach. Bonds are valued at the closing price reported on the active market on which the securities are traded and are considered Level 1. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">F</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">28</font>

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">On </font><font style="display: inline;">December 22, 2010</font><font style="display: inline;">, in connection with the IPO, the Partnership entered into a Credit Agreement along with QRE GP, OLLC as </font><font style="display: inline;">b</font><font style="display: inline;">orrower, and a syndicate of banks (the &#x201C;Credit Agreement&#x201D;).&nbsp; </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">As </font><font style="display: inline;">of December 31, 2013, we had a </font><font style="display: inline;">$950</font><font style="display: inline;"> million borrowing base, $</font><font style="display: inline;">615.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of</font><font style="display: inline;"> borrowings outstanding and $</font><font style="display: inline;">23.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of letters of credit issued</font><font style="display: inline;"> resulting in $</font><font style="display: inline;">311.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;"> of borrowing availability</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">During 2013, our weighted-</font><font style="display: inline;">average interest rate paid on our variable debt obligation</font><font style="display: inline;"> was </font><font style="display: inline;">3.6</font><font style="display: inline;">%, excluding the impact of hedges.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2013, our weighted average-interest on the variable debt obligation was </font><font style="display: inline;">2.2</font><font style="display: inline;">%, excluding the potential impact of hedges. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Commencing with the fourth quarter of 2013, we will distribute to common unitholders on a monthly basis.We intend to continue to make regular cash distributions to unitholders on a monthly or quarterly basis, although there is no assurance as to the future cash distributions since they are dependent upon future earnings, cash flows, capital requirements, financial condition and other factors.&nbsp;Our credit facility prohibits us from making cash distributions if any potential default or event of default, as defined in our credit facility, occurs or would result from the cash distribution.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our partnership agreement requires us to distribute all of our available cash on a </font><font style="display: inline;">monthly or </font><font style="display: inline;">quarterly basis. Our available cash is our cash on hand at the end of a quarter after the payment of our expenses and the establishment of reserves for future capital expenditures and operational needs, including cash from working capital borrowings. We intend to fund a portion of our capital expenditures with additional borrowings or issuances of additional units. We may also borrow to make distributions to unitholders, for example, in circumstances where we believe that the distribution level is sustainable over the long term, but short-term factors have caused available cash from operations to be insufficient to pay the distribution at the current level. Our cash distribution policy reflects a basic judgment that our unitholders will be better served by us distributing our available cash, after expenses and reserves, rather than retaining it.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, 2013, QRE GP owns a </font><font style="display: inline;">0.1%</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">general partner</font><font style="display: inline;"> interest in us, represented by </font><font style="display: inline;">51,036</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">general partner</font><font style="display: inline;"> units. QRE GP has the right, but not the obligation, to contribute a proportionate amount of capital to us to maintain its current </font><font style="display: inline;">general partner</font><font style="display: inline;"> interest. QRE GP&#x2019;s initial 0.1% interest in distributions will be reduced if we issue additional units in the future and QRE GP does not contribute a proportionate share of capital to us to maintain its 0.1% </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">general partnership</font><font style="display: inline;"> interest. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The QRE GP, LLC Long-Term Incentive Plan (the &#x201C;Plan&#x201D;) was established for employees, officers, consultants and directors of QRE GP and its affiliates, including QRM, who perform services for us. The Plan consists of unit options, restricted units, phantom units, unit appreciation rights, distribution equivalent rights, other unit-based awards and unit awards. The purpose of awards under the Plan is to provide additional incentive compensation to such individuals providing services to us and to align the economic interests of such individuals with the interests of our unitholders. The Plan limits the number of common units that may be delivered pursuant to awards under the Plan to 1.8 million units. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On February 3, 2014 we filed a definitive proxy statement on Form 14/A, which provides information regarding a special meeting of limited partners to be held on March 10, 2014 to hold a unitholder vote on an amendment to our Long-Term Incentive Plan to increase the number of units under the plan by </font><font style="display: inline;">3,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;">. See Note 22 &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Subsequent Events</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Restricted Units </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Periodically we issue restricted units with a service condition (&#x201C;Restricted Units&#x201D;) and restricted units with a market condition (&#x201C;Performance Units&#x201D;). The fair value of the Restricted Units, based on the closing price of our common units at the grant date, is amortized to compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of the award. The fair value of the Performance Units, based on a Monte Carlo model with assumptions based on market conditions, is amortized to compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of the award.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On April 22, 2013, we granted approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">455,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> Restricted Unit awards and approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">149,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> Performance Unit awards to employees of QRM and </font><font style="display: inline;">20,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> unit awards to independent directors of the Partnership.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Service Restricted Units </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">For the </font><font style="display: inline;">years</font><font style="display: inline;"> ended </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, </font><font style="display: inline;">we recognized compensation expense related to the outstanding awards of </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">6.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">3.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">1.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively. As of December 31, 2013, we had </font><font style="display: inline;">754,822</font><font style="display: inline;"> of Restricted Units outstanding with unrecognized grant date fair value compensation expense of $</font><font style="display: inline;">10.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, which we expect to be recognized over a weighted-average period of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">1.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of unrecognized compensation expense does not necessarily represent the amount that will ultimately be recognized by us in our statements of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Performance Restricted Units.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">F</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">39</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">The performance awards will be earned over a three year period based on the Partnership&#x2019;s performance relative to its peers</font><font style="display: inline;"> in accordance with the Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;The final shares to be issued will range from </font><font style="display: inline;">0</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;">225</font><font style="display: inline;">% of the initial shares granted. For Performance Units, we recognize compensation expense using a straight-line amortization of the grant date fair value over the performance </font><font style="display: inline;">period. For the years ended December 31, 2013 and 2012, we recognized compensation expense related to the outstanding awards of $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2013, we had </font><font style="display: inline;">267,489</font><font style="display: inline;"> of Performance Units outstanding with unrecognized grant date fair value compensation expense of $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, which we expect to be recognized over a weighted-average period of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">1.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of unrecognized compensation expense does not necessarily represent the amount that will ultimately be recognized by us in our statements of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The following assumptions were</font><font style="display: inline;"> used for the Performance Units</font><font style="display: inline;"> based on market conditions using a Monte Carlo model to</font><font style="display: inline;"> estimate the grant date fair</font><font style="display: inline;"> value </font><font style="display: inline;">of </font><font style="display: inline;">the awards. The four primary inputs for the Monte Carlo model are the risk-free rate, volatility of returns, correlation in movement of total unitholder return relative to a relevant peer group and the expected distribution rate. Risk-free rate was based on the Federal Reserve for treasuries equal to the remaining duration of the performance period</font><font style="display: inline;">, which was </font><font style="display: inline;">0.4</font><font style="display: inline;">% for the 2013 and 2012 grants</font><font style="display: inline;">. Volatility was determined based on the annualized daily </font><font style="display: inline;">historical </font><font style="display: inline;">volatility</font><font style="display: inline;">, which was </font><font style="display: inline;">approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">29%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the 2013 grants and ranged from </font><font style="display: inline;">31%</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">32%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the 2012 grants</font><font style="display: inline;">. Correlation in movement of total unitholder return was determined based on a correlation matrix that was created which identifies total shareholder return correlations for each pair of companies in the peer group, including the </font><font style="display: inline;">Partnership</font><font style="display: inline;">. The paired returns in the correlati</font><font style="display: inline;">on matrix ranged from </font><font style="display: inline;">33.7</font><font style="display: inline;">% to </font><font style="display: inline;">56.6</font><font style="display: inline;">% for the </font><font style="display: inline;">Partnership</font><font style="display: inline;"> and its peer group. The expected distribution</font><font style="display: inline;"> rate</font><font style="display: inline;"> is calculated using a trailing six month average for the </font><font style="display: inline;">Partnership</font><font style="display: inline;"> and its peer group as of the date of grant</font><font style="display: inline;">, which was </font><font style="display: inline;">11</font><font style="display: inline;">% and </font><font style="display: inline;">10%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the 2013 and 2012 grants</font><font style="display: inline;">. Based on these inputs discussed above, a ranking was projected identifying the </font><font style="display: inline;">Partnership</font><font style="display: inline;">'s rank relative to the peer group for each award period which determines the anticipated payout.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;The weighted average grant date fair value per unit, using the method described above, was </font><font style="display: inline;">$10.03</font><font style="display: inline;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;">10.35</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the years ended December 31, 2013 and 2012, respectively, and is being recognized ratably in expense over the service period.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On December 22, 2010, in connection with the closing of the </font><font style="display: inline;">IPO</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">we entered into the</font><font style="display: inline;"> Services Agreement with QRM, </font><font style="display: inline;">QRE GP</font><font style="display: inline;"> and OLLC, pursuant to which QRM will provide the administrative and acquisition advisory services necessary to allow </font><font style="display: inline;">QRE GP</font><font style="display: inline;"> to manage, operate and grow </font><font style="display: inline;">our </font><font style="display: inline;">business. </font><font style="display: inline;">We</font><font style="display: inline;"> do not have any employees. The Services Agreement requires that employees of </font><font style="display: inline;">QRM</font><font style="display: inline;"> (including the persons who are executive officers of </font><font style="display: inline;">QRE GP)</font><font style="display: inline;"> devote such portion of their time as may be reasonable and ne</font><font style="display: inline;">cessary for the operation of our</font><font style="display: inline;"> business. The executive officers of </font><font style="display: inline;">QRE GP</font><font style="display: inline;"> currently devote a majority of their time</font><font style="display: inline;"> to</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">our</font><font style="display: inline;"> business, and </font><font style="display: inline;">we</font><font style="display: inline;"> expect them to continue to do so for the foreseeable future.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Under the Services Agreement, from the closing of the </font><font style="display: inline;">IPO</font><font style="display: inline;"> through December 31, 2012, QRM </font><font style="display: inline;">was </font><font style="display: inline;">entitled to a quarterly administrative services fee equal to </font><font style="display: inline;">3.5</font><font style="display: inline;">% of the Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="display: inline;">, as defined by the Services Agreement,</font><font style="display: inline;"> generated by </font><font style="display: inline;">us</font><font style="display: inline;"> during the preceding quarter, calculated prior to the payment of the fee. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Beginning on January 1, 2013, QRM became entitled to a quarterly reimbursement of general and administrative charges based on the allocation of charges between the Fund and us based on the estimated use of such services by each party.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fee included direct expenses plus an allocation of compensation costs based on employee time expended and other indirect expenses based on multiple operating metrics.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the Fund raises a second fund, the quarterly administrative services costs will be further divided to include the second fund as well.&nbsp;&nbsp;QRM will have discretion to determine in good faith the proper allocation of the charges pursuant to the Services Agreement.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Omnibus Agreement </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On December&nbsp;22, 2010, in connection with the closing of </font><font style="display: inline;">our</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">IPO</font><font style="display: inline;">, we entered i</font><font style="display: inline;">nto an Omnibus Agreement (the &#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">Omnibus Agreement&#x201D;) </font><font style="display: inline;">by and among us</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">QRE GP, </font><font style="display: inline;">OLLC, </font><font style="display: inline;">the Fund, the Predecessor and </font><font style="display: inline;">QA Global.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the terms of the Omnibus Agreement, the Fund will offer </font><font style="display: inline;">us</font><font style="display: inline;"> the </font><font style="display: inline;">first option</font><font style="display: inline;"> to purchase properties that it may offer for sale, so long as the properties consist of at least </font><font style="display: inline;">70</font><font style="display: inline;">% proved developed producing reserves. The 70% threshold is a value-weighted determination made by the Fund. Additionally, the Fund will allow </font><font style="display: inline;">us</font><font style="display: inline;"> to participate in acquisition opportunities to the </font><font style="display: inline;">extent </font><font style="display: inline;">that it invests</font><font style="display: inline;"> any of the remaining</font><font style="display: inline;"> approximately</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;$</font><font style="display: inline;">113.2</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million of its equity capital</font><font style="display: inline;"> or acquires reserves as follow-on investments that are associated with its existing reserves</font><font style="display: inline;">. Specifically, the Fund will offer </font><font style="display: inline;">us</font><font style="display: inline;"> the </font><font style="display: inline;">first opportunity</font><font style="display: inline;"> to participate in at least </font><font style="display: inline;">25</font><font style="display: inline;">% of each acquisition opportunity available to it, so long as at least 70% of the allocated value is attributable to proved developed producing reserves.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> These contractual obligations will remain in effect </font><font style="display: inline;">until December 21, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>

The Fund indemnification obligation will (i)&nbsp;survive for one year after the closing of </font><font style="display: inline;">our IPO</font><font style="display: inline;"> with respect to title, and (ii)&nbsp;terminate upon the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations with respect to income taxes. </font><font style="display: inline;">We</font><font style="display: inline;"> will indemnify the Fund against certain potential environmental claims, losses and expenses associated with the operation of </font><font style="display: inline;">our</font><font style="display: inline;"> business that arise after the consummation of </font><font style="display: inline;">our IPO</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">management incentive fee paid to our general partner for the quarter immediately preceding the quarter for which such fee is to be converted and the management incentive fee payable to our general partner for the quarter for which such fee is to be converted, divided by (b) the cash distribution per unit for the most recently completed quarter. </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">We refer to such conversion as a &#x201C;Conversion Election.&#x201D; The reduction in the management incentive fee as a result of any conversion will directly offset the increase in distributions required by the newly issued Class B units.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">In the event of such Conversion Election, unless we experience a change of control, our general partner will not be permitted to exercise the Conversion Election again until (i) the completion of the fourth full calendar quarter following the previous Conversion Election and (ii) the Gross Management Incentive Fee Base has increased to 115% of the Gross Management Incentive Fee Base as of the immediately preceding conversion date. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Third Party Reserves Estimate.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The reserve estimates as of December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;">2013, </font><font style="display: inline;">201</font><font style="display: inline;">2 and 2011</font><font style="display: inline;"> presented in the table below were based on reserve reports prepared by </font><font style="display: inline;">Netherland, Sewell &amp; Associates, Inc. for 2013 and </font><font style="display: inline;">Miller &amp; Lents, Ltd.</font><font style="display: inline;"> for 2012 and 2011</font><font style="display: inline;">, independent reserve engineers, using FASB and SEC rules in effect a</font><font style="display: inline;">s of</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Oil and Natural Gas Reserve Quantities. </font><font style="display: inline;">Proved oil and natural gas reserves are the estimated quantities of crude oil and natural gas that geological and engineering data demonstrate, with reasonable certainty, to be recoverable in future years from known reservoirs under existing economic and operating conditions (i.e., prices and costs) existing at the time the estimate is made.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Prices include consideration of changes in existing prices provided only by contractual arrangement, but not on escalations based on future conditions. All of the Partnership&#x2019;s oil and natural gas producing activities were conducted within the continental United States.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Proved developed oil and natural gas reserves are reserves that can be expected to be recovered through existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods. Additional oil and natural gas expected to be obtained through the application of fluid injection or other improved recovery techniques for supplementing the natural forces and mechanisms of primary recovery are included as &#x201C;proved developed reserves&#x201D; only after testing by a pilot project or after the operations of an installed program has confirmed through production response that the increased recovery will be achieved.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We emphasize that reserve estimates are inherently imprecise and that estimates of new discoveries and undeveloped locations are more imprecise than estimates of established producing oil and gas properties. Accordingly, these estimates are expected to change as future information becomes available.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our total proved reserves have increased each year since 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;The extensions in our reserves during 2013 are primarily attributable to additional development opportunities at Jay Field resulting from updated technical analysis.&nbsp;&nbsp;The revisions in our reserves during 2013 are primarily attributable to favorable prices and enhanced performance partially offset by a reduction in PUD reserves. The acquisitions of our reserves are primarily due to the 2013 East Texas Oil Field acquisition.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Net Cash Flows</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Standardized Measure represents the present value of estimated future cash inflows from proved oil and natural gas reserves, less future development, production, plugging and abandonment costs, discounted at 10% per annum to reflect timing of future cash flows. Production costs do not include depreciation, depletion and amortization of capitalized acquisition, exploration and development costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our estimated proved reserves and related future net revenues and Standardized Measure were determined using index prices for oil and natural gas, without giving effect to derivative transactions, and were held constant throughout the life of the properties. The unweighted arithmetic average first-day of-the-month prices for the prior 12 months were $96.91/Bbl for oil and $3.67/MMbtu for natural gas as of December 31, 2013; $94.71/Bbl for oil and $2.76/MMbtu for natural gas as of December 31, 2012; and $96.19/Bbl for oil and $4.12/MMbtu for natural gas as of December 31, 2011. These prices were adjusted by lease for quality, transportation fees, geographical differentials, marketing bonuses or deductions and other factors affecting the price received at the wellhead. As of December 31, 2013, the relevant average realized prices for oil, natural gas and NGLs were $101.75 per Bbl, $3.60 per Mcf and $40.36 per Bbl. As of December 31, 2012, the relevant average realized prices for oil, natural gas and NGLs were $96.86 per Bbl, $2.81</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">per Mcf and $42.16</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">per Bbl.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, the relevant average realized prices for oil, natural gas and NGLs were $93.69 per Bbl, $4.28</font><font style="display: inline;"> per Mcf</font><font style="display: inline;"> and $50.00 per Bbl. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Changes in the demand for oil and natural gas, inflation and other factors make such estimates inherently imprecise and subject to substantial revision. This table should not be construed to be an estimate of current market value of our proved reserves.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
